intro: Lesson 27: Sand, clay and loam. To understand how sand, clay and loam soils are different

head: Sand
Clay
rows: Can be rolled into a sausage

questions.q: A soil feels gritty and water runs through fast. Which soil is it?
questions.model: Clue 1: gritty means big grains. Clue 2: water runs through fast means big gaps. Big grains and gaps: sand.

questions.q: A soil rolls into a smooth sausage. Which soil?
Which soil is best for most plants?
Do the feel test on two soils (garden soil, compost, play sand or pot soil). Fill in the table: colour, feel, does it roll?
questions.a: Sensible observations, e.g. play sand: light, gritty, does not roll; compost: dark, crumbly
questions.model: Teacher tests play sand on camera and fills in the first row: 'light brown, gritty, does not roll'.

questions.q: Sieve one soil. What stayed in the sieve? What fell through?
questions.a: Stones, roots and twigs stay; fine soil falls through

questions.q: Why do gardeners add compost to clay soil?
questions.a: Compost adds humus, which makes clay more crumbly so water and roots get through.
A mixture of sand, clay and humus
options: A mixture of sand, clay and humus

questions.q: Big question: why does damp sand make a sandcastle?
questions.a: A little water sticks the grains together.
